Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Bounded transport recording and strict replay

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

This optional package records a borrowed Transport interface and replays its observations without opening a real endpoint. It records send attempts/results, receive capacity/results/payloads, polling, status, connectivity, generation queries and close. Nil callbacks remain nil: fallback status and generation behavior stays with the ordinary Transport helpers. Payload bytes are copied into owned storage.

Odin
log: trace.Log
assert(trace.init(&log))
capture: trace.Capture
wire := trace.capture(&capture, &log, existing_transport)
// Use wire with the normal caller. Caller marks can record clock/configuration.
trace.mark(&log, 1, now_ms)

The default limits retain up to one million events and 64 MiB of payloads. Reaching capacity or failing an allocation stops recording without changing underlying sends, receives, or return values. The resulting incomplete log cannot be encoded or replayed as a complete record. Recording adds allocation and copy work, so account for that cost when measuring the wrapped system.

Destroying the log releases its storage only; closing through the wrapper forwards to the endpoint. The caller controls capture/log lifetime and must stop using borrowed handles before destroying them.

encode writes a versioned canonical representation, independent of native padding and endianness. decode checks limits before allocation, validates entry/payload bounds and preserves the destination on failure. Its digest detects corruption; it is not authentication. Packet payloads can contain credentials or private game data. Treat recordings accordingly and share only authorized test data.

replay exposes the same callback presence and returns recorded observations. It checks operation order, destinations/channels, outbound bytes, and receive buffer capacity. On a mismatch, it retains the first error and its cursor position. finished requires the entire record to be consumed without error. User marks can describe pump times and configuration; next_mark looks ahead and read_mark consumes one. Do not mutate or destroy a log while replay borrows it.

To reproduce a caller, restore its configuration, model, clocks, local inputs, and other external decisions alongside the transport log. Strict replay returns recorded observations and checks that the caller makes the same calls; it does not compute new server responses when outbound traffic changes. A different harness can replay only incoming data, but that does not establish the same call-sequence agreement.

The Claimball observer fixture uses marks for client configuration and each actual pump time, then checks state/effect hashes against a standalone replay. This keeps Godot rendering and live ENet scheduling out of receiver reproduction.
